notes_for_editor: Three sources name a Pecan City tower, but none describes it: tnlandforms.us row GA102 (coordinates, elevation 255 with no unit, no codes); the Eastern US Lookouts Georgia list, which gives only the name and county and is undated; and its Pretoria entry, which has a March 1931 note on a tower near Albany, 60 feet high on a 20-foot hill, that its own note says may be the Pecan City tower. The identity is the main open question; the story reports it as unresolved and does not claim a build date. Wikipedia gives the community's coordinates as 31.51778, -84.07, about 2 km from the tnlandforms tower point; the story uses the tower point and does not cite the Wikipedia coordinates. Searches: a Pecan City fire tower and Forestry Commission history query found no tower record, and a query on the Pine Island Timber Protective Organization and 1931 tower found nothing relevant. An Albany Herald piece returned a 403 and was not read. Not on NHLR or the Former Fire Lookout Sites Georgia lists. The story is about 190 words, within the range. No photos. Next checks if time allows: Georgia Forestry Commission Dougherty County records, Albany newspapers from 1931 for the Pine Island tower, Georgia Archives. If an Albany-area source ties the 1931 tower to a named site, this entry's build, staffing and fate can be rewritten.
